newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-S&P places ANI on negative watch.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-S&P places ANI on negative watch.

text.p: Standard and Poor's Corp said it has placed Australian National Industries Ltd's (ANI) BBB long-term credit rating on creditwatch with negative implications and has affirmed its A-3 short-term rating.

S&P said the creditwatch placement followed the release of ANI's fiscal 1996 results which showed a failure to improve margins and profitability in core manufacturing and distribution businesses and further losses in Holter, its environmental engineering business.

"Holter's results have fallen well short of expectations in the half year to June 30, 1996, as a result of cost over-runs, technical difficulties, further delays in commissioning of waste-to-energy plants and a deterioration in environmental engineering markets," S&P said in a statement.
ANI earlier reported a net loss of A$213.19 million for the year to June 30, 1996 after recording an abnormal loss of A$198.55 million.

The ratings agency said ANI's leverage and cash flow-to-debt remained weak for a company with its credit rating despite the reduction of its debt following the A$136 million floatation of its Coates Hire business.
"ANI's gearing has been adversely affected by further substantial write-downs in relation to Holter's ongoing difficulties," S&P said.
S&P said if it decided to adjust ANI's credit rating, it was still likely to remain investment grade.
